Lynch scales for ggplot2

Source: R/scales.R
scale_colour_lynch_d.Rd

Colour and fill scales using the Lynch palettes. The `_d` scales are for categories and use a discrete palette from [lynch_palettes]; the `_c` scales are for numbers and use a ramp from [lynch_sequential] or [lynch_diverging].

scale_colour_lynch_d(palette = "lost_highway", direction = 1, ...)

scale_fill_lynch_d(palette = "lost_highway", direction = 1, ...)

scale_colour_lynch_c(
  palette = "dune",
  type = c("sequential", "diverging"),
  direction = 1,
  midpoint = NULL,
  ...
)

scale_fill_lynch_c(
  palette = "dune",
  type = c("sequential", "diverging"),
  direction = 1,
  midpoint = NULL,
  ...
)

scale_color_lynch_d(palette = "lost_highway", direction = 1, ...)

scale_color_lynch_c(
  palette = "dune",
  type = c("sequential", "diverging"),
  direction = 1,
  midpoint = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

palette

Name of the palette. For the discrete scales, any name in `names(lynch_palettes)`; the `_safe` palettes stay distinct with red-green colour blindness. For the continuous scales, a name in `names(lynch_sequential)` or `names(lynch_diverging)`, depending on `type`.

direction

`1` for the palette's order, `-1` to reverse it.

...

Other arguments passed to [ggplot2::discrete_scale()] or [ggplot2::continuous_scale()], such as `name`, `labels` or `na.value`.

type

`"sequential"` for ordered values, `"diverging"` for values either side of a midpoint.

midpoint

For continuous scales, the data value to put at the centre of the ramp, such as `0` for a diverging scale. `NULL` spans the data range.

Value

A ggplot2 scale.

Examples

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_lynch_d("twin_peaks_safe")


ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_lynch_c("dune")


df <- data.frame(x = 1:20, y = 1, change = seq(-5, 14))
ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = change)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_lynch_c("mulholland_drive", type = "diverging", midpoint = 0)
